3. Brief facts leading to this appeal are as follows:
The marriage between the petitioner and respondent no.1 was solemnized in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals on 29.01.2001.
The Nuptial was arranged on the date of marriage at the residence of the petitioner at No.11, Someshwara temple street, Ulsoor, Bengaluru.
On the very first night, the respondent no.1 declined to spend time and co-habit with her on the pretext of having high fever.
On the next day also, the respondent no.1 refused to co- habit with the petitioner.

After 2 days of the marriage, the respondents prepared to leave Bengaluru to Purucherry on 31.01.2001 without taking the petitioner with them and after a great deal of persuasion, agreed to take her along with him.

After reaching Puducherry, the respondent no.1 did not stay with her or spend time with her and he maintained distance with her and treated as a complete stranger and she was made to stay away and sleep separately along with his parents.
The petitioner stayed for about 20 days at Puducherry from 1.11.2001 to 20.11.2001.

During these days,
the respondent No.1 stayed away from the petitioner.
After 20 days, while the petitioner was returning to Bengaluru, the respondents specifically instructed that she should return Puducherry only after obtaining transfer of her employment.
Further she was instructed not even to visit Puducherry for any short visit and she returned back to Bengaluru and reported for duty and her relation with respondent no.1 remained unconsummated.
Thereafter she continued to stay along with her parents at Bengaluru.

After she returned to Bengaluru, the respondent no.1 severed all sort R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/
2 of communication from his end, though she tried to contact with respondent no.1 with great difficulty over phone.
The respondents did not enquire about her willingness or wellness.
Thereafter respondent no.1 was transferred to Cuddalore during the month of June 2002.
Respondent no.1 never intimated this aspect to the petitioner.
When she enquired with respondent no.1, he had informed her that his deputation to Cuddalore was for a short period and that he would get permanent transfer to Puducherry.
Respondent no.1 further assured that till such time she had to stay at Bengaluru with her parents.

On believing the version of respondent no.1 and as advised by him, she initiated the process of seeking her transfer to Puducherry and accordingly, she submitted her application on 27.01.2013 for expediting her transfer to Puducherry.
In the meanwhile, she learnt that the respondent no.1 had been transferred to Punganur, Andhra Pradesh.
Being frustrated about this deliberate act of the respondent on 23.08.2004, she along with her parents went to Punganur and met respondent no.1 at his bank.
Respondent no.1 asked her to wait till he seeks transfer to Puducherry.
On 4.4.2005, her transfer orders were issued and she was posted to Thindivanam Head Post Office within the jurisdiction of Puducherry division.

Though the complainant reported for her duty at Thindivanam which was just one hour journey by road from the matrimonial home at Puducherry, the parents-in-law of the petitioner refused to accommodate her in their house.
It was also told that the respondent no.1 not being at home since his transfer orders have not been issued, it was not appropriate for them to keep her at the matrimonial house.

The petitioner finding no other alternate had to make her own arrangements and accordingly, took admission in a working women hostel at No. 84, Sundaramastry street, Kosapalyam, Puducherry and started staying there.
In the meanwhile, the respondent no.1 was transferred from Punganur to Proddadur in A.P. on 4.9.2007 which was not informed to the petitioner.
She met the respondent no.1 at Prodaddur and again pleaded him to set up the matrimonial home at Proddadur and to lead a married life.

After the petitioner came to know the transfer of respondent no.1 to Puducherry, she called her parents to Puducherry who immediately joined her and thereafter they went to the residence of respondent no.1 and enquired about the next course of action for resuming her married life.

The respondents further gained three months time on the reason of constructing an additional accommodation on the first floor of the residential house of respondent no.1 and the petitioner could join the respondent no.1 thereafter.
It was further instructed that till such time, she should continue staying at the working women hostel.
Thereafter it was only on 6.2.2009, she was allowed to enter the newly constructed portion of the matrimonial home.
The parents of the petitioner furnished the house with all household utensils, almirah, cot, bet, water purifier, stove etc.

On the next day of she entering her marital house, the respondents on the pretext of safety, took all the jewelleries weighing about 136 grams of gold and silver items weighing totally about 870 grams of silver belonging to the complainant promising to keep the same in the safe custody of the bank locker.
The petitioner on return from her office, she was forced to confine herself to the first floor.

As soon as she entering the first floor, the respondents used to lock the gate which was provided in the first floor from outside and the said gate was opened only in the morning 8 a.m making no room even to mingle with her neighbouring family members.
The respondent no.1 continued to stay with his parents in the ground floor along with his sister and daughter of his sister.

It is further alleged that ever since the petitioner started staying at the residence of respondent no.1, he insisted and received a sum of Rs.10,000/- every from her out of her net salary of Rs. 13,000/-.

The respondent no.1 thus collected a total sum of Rs. 1,36,000/- from the petitioner and in the month of March 2009 demanded further sum of Rs. 60,000/- on the pretext of payment of income tax and parents R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/
3 of the respondent No.1 requested her to arrange a sum of Rs. 50,000/- for purchasing colour TV,
washing machine, refrigerator and wet grinder.
She has further contended that she had expressed her intention of returning to Bengaluru.
At that time, the respondent 1 threatened that she would not be allowed to leave the matrimonial home.

Thereafter, she had informed her parents, who immediately rushed to Puducherry on 5.6.2010 and the petitioner and her parents went to All Women police station in Puducherry and lodged a complaint seeking for their protection enabling her to leave Puducherry and come to Bengaluru.

The petitioner and her parents being highly apprehensive of the safety of the petitioner left Puducherry who had stayed in Hotel Danaa Orchid,
at Puducherry and returned to Bengaluru on the next day.
The respondents have deliberately exerted all unbearable cruelty on the petitioner and with deliberate intention of coercing her to meet their illegal and endless greed.
The marriage of the petitioner has not consummated even as on that day and her life deliberately ruined by respondent no.1 and his parents.
Hence, prayed for allowing the petition.
4. The lower court called for the domestic incident report and issued notice to the respondents.
The respondent no.1 has filed his objection and in his objection, he has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
The lower court has no jurisdiction to try the petition.
The fabricated version of the petitioner just to put pressure on the respondent no.1 to yield to the demands of the petitioner and her father.
He has denied all the allegations made in the complaint.
He has denied that the petitioner is residing at Bengaluru.
The petitioner has gained employment as postal Asst. at Head Post Office, Puducherry.

He has contended that it was the petitioner who at the very first night of the marriage disclosed to the respondent no.1 that she was suffering from some gynecological problems and was unable to perform conjugal duties and emotionally forced him to give a promise that he will not going to disclose the physical weakness suffering by her to anybody.

The respondent no.1 has sacrificed his want of pleasure by not insisting upon the petitioner to perform her conjugal duties just to ensure her that he is not going to force her either psychologically or physically without her willingness to cooperate.
Even on several occasions, the respondent no.1 requested the petitioner to go for a thorough medical check up so as to diagnose that what is the physical problem she was really facing.
But the petitioner blatantly refused to undergo any medical check up and treatment.
The petitioner was never denied permission to go to her parent's house and he never expressed his unwillingness to take the petitioner whenever wanted to go.

He has denied that the petitioner got her transfer from Bengaluru to Thindivanam a near place to Pondicherry as per the instructions of the respondents and if these allegations were true, then she had no impediment in applying for a transfer even as early as 2001 immediately after the marriage.
He has denied that the petitioner was prevented from entering the matrimonial house.
He has denied that the petitioner was living in a hostel at Puducherry while she was serving at Thindivanam.

She started living in a hostel at Puducherry much against the wishes of the respondent no.1 just for the reason that she might have to take care of respondent No.2 and 3 who are aged 83 and 70 years old respectively.
The respondent No.3 is suffering a rare ailment of the bone which has rendered her almost immobile and requires an attendant always even for the personal needs.

The respondent No.4 was the one who was taking care of the respondent No.3 as well as the household chores and the petitioner would not be required to do anything for the family of the respondent No.1.

He has further denied that the petitioner was made to stay alone on the first floor and in fact the first floor of the matrimonial home belongs to one Shivasubramanian, the younger brother of respondent no.1.

He has denied the demand made by them during the time of marriage.

He has further contended that the expenses for the wedding were borne out by them and their family as per their custom prevailed and in fact the first respondent and his brother had taken a loan to meet the wedding expenses.
The actual reason for non co-habiting was solely due to the petitioner.

He has further contended that once the respondent No.1 got transferred to Puducherry in 2008, he requested the petitioner to join him at the matrimonial house which was then only a single storied structure, but upon the insistence of the petitioner that she would stay only in an independent portion, the respondents and his family had no option but to construct a portion on the first floor to meet the demand of the petitioner.
He has denied that the petitioner has not taken away all her belongings on 6.6.2010.

He has contended that the petitioner has misused process of law and filed this false petition so as to harass him and his family members mentally and physically and hence,
prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Before the lower court, the petitioner herself examined as P.w.1 and got marked Ex.P1 to 133.
The respondent no.1 himself examined as R.w.1 and two independent witnesses have been examined as R.w.2 and 3 and got marked Ex.R1 to R8.
After hearing the learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent, the lower court passed an order dismissing the petition filed by the petitioner.

6. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned order, the petitioner has filed an appeal contending that the impugned order being cryptic without any reason is arbitrary, capricious and illegal and same requires to be set aside.

The learned Magistrate has not adverted to various undisputed factual aspect of the matter which categorically establishes the exertion of sexual violence, verbal and emotional and economical violence and dowry related harassment by the respondents to the appellant.

Except selectively extracting the facts narrated in the petition, the learned Magistrate has not appreciated and applied judicious mind into the factual aspect of the matter which categorically establishes the violence exerted on the appellant.
The very concept of domestic violence has been disregarded by the learned Magistrate.
The learned Magistrate has lost sight of the very psychological aspect of the violence which is essential element in promulgation of the special legislation.

The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate the very purpose of the special legislation in that a person who is married for 8 years was not allowed to stay in her matrimonial house despite having made several sacrifices.
The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate that from the inception of the marriage, the respondent no.1 did not cohabit with the appellant.
The appellant made a number of attempts to join the respondent no.1 and to lead happy married life.
The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate this extremely insensitive and inhuman behaviour of the respondent no.1 in considering the psychological violence exerted by the respondent no.1.

The learned Magistrate failed to appreciate that the appellant herein being determined to lead a matrimonial life had gone to Puducherry and was forced to live in a working women hostel for a period of over four years.
The respondent no.1 being completely aware of this had not even paid a visit to her thereby completely neglecting the very existence of the appellant.
The learned Magistrate has not taken this crucial aspect of the matter into consideration.

The respondent no.1 who was legally, morally and ethically obligated to provide emotional and physical protection to the appellant R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/
5 had shattered all the hopes of the appellant on account of non consummation of marriage.

Hence,
prayed for setting aside the impugned order passed by the lower court.

The respondent has appeared before this court through his counsel and this court secured the lower court records.

17. On perusal of the pleadings as well as evidence, it is clear that admittedly, the petitioner is the legally wedded wife of the respondent no.1 and respondent nos. 2 to 4 are the parents-in-law and sister-in-law of the petitioner.
The petitioner was the resident of Bengaluru and respondents were the residents of Pondicherry, Tamil nadu.
At the time of marriage, the petitioner was an employee of postal department and respondent was an employee of Indian bank.
Admittedly, the marriage between the petitioner and respondent no.1 has not been consummated.
There is no specific allegation in the complaint as well as in the evidence of any physical violence or cruelty having been committed by the respondents on the petitioner.
It is the allegation of the petitioner that there is a deprivation of sexual intimacy by the respondent no.1 on account of impotency.

The petitioner has filed petition u/s 12 ((1) (a) and 13 (1) (i) (a) of Hindu Marriage Act for decree of nullity and for decree of divorce against the respondent no.1 and admittedly, the said M.C.No.2496/2010 filed by the petitioner came to be allowed and it is declared that the marriage of the petitioner is nullity and dissolved by a decree of divorce.
18.

Therefore, during the pendency of the said appeal, I don't want to comment on the findings recorded in the said petition.

It is the case of the petitioner that the respondent no.1 has been avoiding to have physical intimacy with her in spite of her several requests and demands to that effect and marriage has not been consummated.
But in this case, there is no medical report to the effect that the respondent no.1 is impotent.
The petitioner has contended that due to deprivation of physical intimacy, she suffered mental cruelty at the hands of respondent no.1.

sentences.text: The respondent no.1 has specifically denied each and every allegations made by the petitioner including the cruelty committed by him and demand of money and non return of household articles and jewels.
This is a petition filed by the petitioner alleging that there is sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, economic abuse.

So, burden is heavily on the petitioner to prove and establish that the respondent no.1 is having physical infirmity i.e. impotency and thereby the petitioner is deprived of sexual intimacy with the respondent no.1.

Except the bare testimony of the petitioner, she has not examined any independent evidence and she has not produced any medical report stating that the respondent no.1 purposefully kept away from her without consummation of marriage due to impotency.
19. It is the case of the petitioner that as per the demand made by the respondent no.1, her father gave Rs.50,000/- by way of D.D.
In this case, the petitioner has produced bank challan marked at Ex.P115 and Xerox copy of D.D.

But the respondent no.1 has examined one Srimathi, the Chief Manager of Indian Bank, Ulsoor branch and she has produced the cheque of the petitioner and the bank challan and statement of account of the petitioner as well as the respondent no.1.
All these documents are marked as Ex.R1 to 6.

Ex.R5 is the cheque issued by the petitioner for Rs. 50,150/- in favour of the bank so as to obtain D.D. and Ex.R6 is the challan written by the father of the petitioner V.T. Rajendran requesting the bank to issue D.D. in the name of petitioner R.Vanitha.
The petitioner gave cheque to the bank for the purpose of obtaining D.D. in her name and not in the name of the respondent no.1.
The bank statement Ex.R1 and R2 does not disclose that the said D.D. was encashed by respondent no.1.
Therefore, there is no evidence on record to show that the petitioner's father gave Rs.50,000/- by way of D.D. to respondent no.1 as demanded by him.
Therefore, the contention that the petitioner's father paid Rs.50,000/- to the respondent no.1 as per his demand falsifies.
20. In so far as jewellery and other articles claimed to have been given to the petitioner by her parents at the time of marriage, she has marked bills at Ex.P4 to 11.

But Ex.P4 to 11 are only estimates, not the actual receipts for purchase of the articles and petitioner has not examined the author of Ex.P4 to 11 to show that the petitioner has purchased the jewels at the time of her marriage.
It is the contention of the petitioner that they have spent Rs.5 lakhs for marriage expenses and she has produced 2 bills marked as Ex.P112 and 113.
Ex.P112 is the receipt issued by Kalyan mantap towards rent for marriage hall and said receipt is for Rs.20,000/-.
Ex.P113 is the receipt for Rs.15,000/- towards hire charges of chairs, vessels etc.

So, as per these two documents, it is clear that the petitioner has spent only Rs.35,000/- for the marriage expenses and no documents have been produced by the petitioner to show that they have spent Rs.5 lakhs for the marriage expenses.
In her evidence, she has deposed that only 20 persons have attended from the side of respondents and 300 persons have attended on their side.

Therefore, it cannot be said that the petitioner has spent Rs.5 lakhs for the marriage expenses and therefore, she cannot claim Rs.5 lakhs from the R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/
11 respondents.
21.
During the course of evidence, she has admitted that respondent no.1 himself brought thali at the time of marriage and also gold ring to her brother.
She has further admitted that they have not returned the said gold ring to the respondent no.1.
During the course of cross-examination, she has deposed that in the month of June 2010, when she left the matrimonial house, she had doubted the impotency of respondent no.1.
It means the petitioner has doubted the impotency of the respondent no.1 in the month of June 2010.
But in her pleadings, she has deposed that at the first day of the marriage, the respondent no.1 has not made physical intimacy with her on the pretext that he was not well.
She has further deposed that she has not intimated to her parents regarding her doubt of impotency of respondent no.1 till June 2010.
She has further deposed that she has not mentioned that the respondent no.1 is impotent in the complaint filed before the police.
She has further deposed that after she brought the household articles from the house of respondent no.1, she did not go to the police station.

If really, the petitioner has left valuables in the house of respondent no.1 or the respondent no.1 refused to give back the valuables, definitely the petitioner would have lodged the complaint before the police station.
She has clearly admitted that she has not issued any notice to respondent no.1 requesting him to hand over her valuables.
Further she has deposed that 1 or 2 times, she and respondent no.1 and her parents-in-law went to temples by hiring a vehicle.
She has further admitted that she has no other document to show that they spent amount for the marriage except Ex.P 112 and 113.
She has further deposed that in the month of December 2009 along with her husband went to Rameshwaram and other places and in the month of March 2010, she and her husband went to Tirupathi.
It means they were in cordial terms till March 2010 and she left her matrimonial house on 6.6.2010.
Therefore, it means the petitioner has made allegations against the respondent regarding impotency without any basis or medical record.
She has also deposed about the ignorance of disability of impotency of respondent no.1 during the course of cross-examination.
It is the case of the respondent no.1 that the petitioner had some gynalogical problem due to which the petitioner did not let the marriage to be consummated.
Therefore, it is clear that both petitioner and respondents are suppressing some facts and not disclosing the truth.
22. Admittedly, the petitioner is drawing monthly salary of Rs.34,143.00 as per Ex.R8.
When she is earning, question of giving maintenance also does not arise.
There is no evidence on record to show that the respondent no.1 took Rs.10,000/- out of her salary every month.
As per Ex.P133, the petitioner was having credit balance of more than Rs.1,25,000/-.

Therefore, except the oral testimony of the petitioner, the petitioner has not produced any document to show the respondents committed cruelty against her and the respondent is having disability of impotency and therefore,
her marriage was not consummated.

The petitioner made allegation against the respondent no.1 that he is having impotency and the respondent no.1 is making allegation against the petitioner that the petitioner is having gynalogical problem.
Therefore, the petitioner should have taken steps to subject the respondent no.1 to medical test.

In the absence of medical evidence, this court cannot come to the conclusion that the respondent no.1 is having a problem of impotency and therefore,
their marriage was not consummated and it amounts to cruelty and sexual abuse.

The petitioner has not proved that she was subjected economic abuse and verbal and emotional abuse from the R.Vanitha vs ) A.Radhakrishnan on 5 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183073143/
12 respondents.
Under these circumstances, the petitioner has failed to prove that she is the victim of domestic violence by the respondents and therefore, she is entitled for the relief claimed in the petition.
23. The lower court on appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence rightly come to the conclusion that the petitioner is not entitled for the relief claimed in the above petition.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, I find no ground to interfere with the findings recorded by the lower court.
The lower court has not committed any error of law and facts in dismissing the petition filed by the petitioner and accordingly, I answer point no.2 to 4 in the negative.
24. Point No.5:

In view of my findings on point Nos. to 4, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal filed by the appellant u/s 29 of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed.

2. The appellant is the petitioner and respondents are husband and parents-in-law and sister-in-law of the petitioner in Crl. Misc. No. 615/2010 on the file of MMTC-1, Bengaluru.

The lower court has no jurisdiction to try the petition.

6. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned order, the petitioner has filed an appeal contending that the impugned order being cryptic without any reason is arbitrary, capricious and illegal and same requires to be set aside.
The learned Magistrate has not adverted to various undisputed factual aspect of the matter which categorically establishes the exertion of sexual violence, verbal and emotional and economical violence and dowry related harassment by the respondents to the appellant.
Except selectively extracting the facts narrated in the petition, the learned Magistrate has not appreciated and applied judicious mind into the factual aspect of the matter which categorically establishes the violence exerted on the appellant.
The very concept of domestic violence has been disregarded by the learned Magistrate.
The learned Magistrate has lost sight of the very psychological aspect of the violence which is essential element in promulgation of the special legislation.
The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate the very purpose of the special legislation in that a person who is married for 8 years was not allowed to stay in her matrimonial house despite having made several sacrifices.
The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate that from the inception of the marriage, the respondent no.1 did not cohabit with the appellant.
The appellant made a number of attempts to join the respondent no.1 and to lead happy married life.
The learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate this extremely insensitive and inhuman behaviour of the respondent no.1 in considering the psychological violence exerted by the respondent no.1.
The learned Magistrate failed to appreciate that the appellant herein being determined to lead a matrimonial life had gone to Puducherry and was forced to live in a working women hostel for a period of over four years.
The respondent no.1 being completely aware of this had not even paid a visit to her thereby completely neglecting the very existence of the appellant.
The petitioner has contended that due to deprivation of physical intimacy, she suffered mental cruelty at the hands of respondent no.1.
for the petitioner has argued that the deprivation of physical intimacy amounts to cruelty and therefore, the petitioner being an aggrieved person can maintain the petition under the provisions of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and there is sexual abuse and economic abuse and further there is an allegation that the respondent no.1 has not returned the household articles and jewels of the petitioner even after the petitioner left the matrimonial home on 6.6.2010.

1) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the relief claimed in the application filed u/s 28 of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 to receive the documents?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that she is the victim of domestic violence by the respondents?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the relief claimed in the petition filed u/s 12 of Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?

5) What order?
(i) To pay Rs.50 lakhs by way of compensation towards mental agony, torture and ruining the life the petitioner.
